correctness.rationale: At zero flux the only real eigenmodes are the normalized dark sines from nontrivial Fourier pairs: dissipativity forces zero trap amplitude, and a pair has exactly one such direction. They also satisfy K_0^* d_k=E_k d_k, so their orthogonal complement reduces K_0 and has strictly negative imaginary spectrum. This justifies algebraic simplicity, not only a one-dimensional eigenspace. At small nonzero total flux Fourier energies are distinct and each plane wave sees the trap, so all modes decay. The two colliding energies have half-gap Delta=(2/n)sin(2pi k/n) phi+O(phi^3) up to sign. Multiplying the rank-one secular equation by (z-mu)^2-Delta^2 gives an analytic equation with z-derivative 2i gamma/n at the dark energy. Its root shift is (n/2)(h(E,0)-i/gamma)Delta^2+O(phi^3), giving the stated decay rate. The leading integrated contribution for each dark branch is its squared projected source amplitude divided by twice that rate. The other branch cross terms are bounded by distinct limiting frequencies, and the fast sector by a uniform finite-dimensional contour estimate. If every dark overlap vanishes, the perturbed slow amplitudes are O(phi), which suffices for bounded lifetime, not merely a zero scaled limit. Parseval on cyclic intervals evaluates the sine sum as a(n-a)/2 for odd n and b(m-b) for even n before the gamma/2 factor. The only zero coefficients are precisely the stated sites. An independent finite-flux Lyapunov calculation corroborated both parities and a bounded antipode with residual below 1.8e-11 in the tested cases.
residual_risks: The finite calculations are corroboration only; the asymptotic proof fixes n, source and positive gamma. Bounded near zero does not itself assert continuity across zero.

evidence: The exact odd-ring work derives the trace formula T=n/kappa+C+kappa B with Fourier-gap sums for arbitrary fixed site source. That derivation uses the Fourier basis, simple energies and equal trap overlaps, not parity. The exact even-ring publication addresses a maximally mixed source, not individual sites. The earlier zero-flux work identifies the same dark-sector absent-overlap sites.
broader_coverage.reasoning: At nonexceptional flux the even ring has the same hypotheses of the Step 2 identities. The mixed-source results check only the average coefficient, and zero-flux dark geometry alone cannot fix the detuned lifetime; the general site-source trace identity is the decisive broader coverage.

evidence: In the exact identity B=(1/n)sum_k y_k g_k, g_k is the sum of inverse energy gaps; y_k is the sum of the same reciprocals weighted by [1-cos(2pi(l-k)a/n)]/n. C consists of sine-weighted single reciprocals. At zero flux the only small gaps are k versus n-k, with magnitude (4/n)|sin(2pi k/n) phi| to first order at J=1.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The two indices in a pair contribute 2[1-cos(4pi ka/n)]/(n^2 (E_k-E_(n-k))^2) to the leading B. Thus kappa B gives gamma/2 times the sine quotient for each pair; C has no inverse-square term. The cyclic sine-sum then gives exactly gamma b(m-b)/2 on an even ring. At a=0 or the even antipode the coalescing-pair source phases coincide identically, so the corresponding terms in C and y vanish. In B the potential simple-pole terms from the pair multiply y_k-y_(n-k), which is O(phi) since the other gaps are regular and their weighted limits agree. Thus the exact identity also supplies boundedness at both exceptional sites. No new even-site spectral formula is needed to imply the stated asymptotic.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Set J=1 and convert population loss kappa to the frozen imaginary onsite coefficient via kappa=2gamma. The magnetic phase is total flux in both models. Multiplication by phi^2 removes the constant and orientation term and leaves the precise frozen odd coefficient; the one-sided orientation convention cannot affect this limit.

evidence: The triangle is an exact special case, not a numerical table; the all-size comparisons are closed spectral sums. With kappa=2gamma and J=1 the mixed even coefficient is gamma(m^2-1)/12.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Averaging gamma b(m-b)/2 over one period in b reproduces gamma(m^2-1)/12. This exact average is corroborating overlap, not an inference of the full position dependence. The frozen finite checks are not evidence of originality.

originality.rationale: A distinct exact odd-ring Resultary formula directly includes every odd-size coefficient and the bounded trap case. More importantly, its Step 2 exact site-source spectral formula uses only equal-magnitude Fourier overlaps and simple energies, with no odd-size assumption. Applying that identity to the even Fourier pairs yields exactly the even site-resolved coefficient and the bounded exceptions; the even publication's mixed-source law alone would not suffice. The frozen proof's use of resonance projectors rather than this identity does not change coverage of the stated lifetime law. This is a mathematical coverage finding, not a determination of chronology from the paths.
residual_risks: The exact odd and mixed even catalogue matches have later path dates; no priority, dependence or order of discovery is inferred. The decisive conclusion is equivalent coverage via the exact identity, not comprehensive historical coverage.

value.rationale: A position-resolved threshold between bounded capture time and a quantitative inverse-square divergence is useful for comparing transport on finite rings. The parity and distance dependence are visible neither from the presence of dark states alone nor from a mixed-source average. The spectral proof explains the separate roles of source overlap and the leakage rate. The judgment of usefulness does not make the mathematically covered law original.
residual_risks: Does not describe a joint large-ring or changing-loss limit, nor an absorption-time distribution.
